title: How to Fix a Squeaky Door Hinge
meta: Stop a squeaky door: tighten hinge screws, pull and clean the hinge pin, lubricate with multipurpose oil or dry graphite, and fix stripped screw holes.
summary: Tighten the hinge screws first, then tap out each hinge pin one at a time, clean it, and coat it with a light multipurpose oil or a dry graphite lubricant before tapping it back in. If a screw spins without tightening, fill the hole with glued wood slivers and redrive it.
causes: Squeaks come from metal rubbing on metal: a dry or rusty hinge pin, or a hinge that has loosened so the leaves rub. Loose screws in the top hinge also let the door sag, which can make it rub the frame.

tools.name: Hammer and nail set (or a thin punch)
tools.note: To tap the hinge pin up

tools.name: Steel wool or fine sandpaper
tools.note: To clean rust off the pin

materials.name: Wood glue and toothpicks or wood slivers

steps.title: Tighten the screws
steps.text: Check every screw in every hinge, on the door and the jamb. Tighten them snugly by hand.

steps.title: Fix any stripped holes
steps.text: If a screw spins, remove it, push a few glue-dipped toothpicks or a wood sliver into the hole, let the glue dry, trim it flush, and redrive the screw. This Old House recommends this method. A longer screw into the framing also works for the top hinge.

steps.title: Pull one hinge pin
steps.text: With the door closed, set a nail set under the pin's head and tap upward. Do one hinge at a time so the door stays in place.

steps.title: Clean and lubricate
steps.text: Wipe the pin clean and rub off rust with steel wool. Coat it lightly with multipurpose oil, or with dry graphite if you want to avoid drips and dust.

steps.title: Reinstall and swing the door
steps.text: Tap the pin back down, wipe off excess oil, and open and close the door several times. Repeat for the other hinges.

safety: Keep a hand on the door when pins are out so it cannot fall.
Protect the floor from oil drips with a rag.
call_pro: The door or frame is cracked or split at the hinges.
The frame has shifted and gaps around the door are getting bigger, which can point to settling.

faq.q: Is WD-40 good for squeaky hinges?
faq.a: A light spray can quiet a hinge for a while, but it is mostly a cleaner and water displacer. A dedicated oil or dry graphite tends to last longer.

faq.q: Why does only one hinge squeak?
faq.a: The top hinge carries the most load as the door pulls away from the frame, so it wears and loosens first.

faq.q: Can I lubricate without removing the pin?
faq.a: You can drip oil at the top of the pin and swing the door, but cleaning the pin works better.
